issues.description: The problem statement gives conflicting requirements for the SealSaloon.stock attribute: one section instructs students to initialize the stock in the SealSaloon constructor as a final (instance) field, while another section explicitly requires that the stock attribute be static (shared across all instances). These two requirements are mutually incompatible (a static field cannot be meaningfully initialized per-instance in the constructor), which will confuse students about whether to implement stock as an instance final field initialized in the constructor or as a static shared field.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the contradiction in the problem statement: either (A) require and document that stock is a static shared field (e.g., declare it static final and initialize it at declaration or in a static block) and remove the instruction to initialize it in the constructor, or (B) require stock to be an instance final field (non-static) and remove the requirement that it be static. Update examples and the UML/notes accordingly so all places consistently describe stock as either static or instance-level. Also ensure the expected visibility (public getter) is stated so students know how to access the shared/instance stock.
